scenes.title: Introduction — stop reading word by word
scenes.narration: P T E Academic Read Aloud. Stop reading word by word. Use five steps: Preview difficult words, Chunk long sentences, Stress key terms, Connect naturally, and Finish clearly. Together, these improve fluency, pronunciation, and reading rhythm.

scenes.title: Step 1 — Preview
scenes.narration: Step one: Preview. Before speaking, identify challenging words. This sentence highlights bioluminescence, organisms, and illumination. Prepare their pronunciation first, so you can read confidently without hesitation.

scenes.title: Step 2 — Chunk
scenes.narration: Step two: Chunk. Follow the coloured phrases: the phenomenon of bioluminescence; observed in certain marine organisms; enables them to produce light; through chemical reactions; without relying on an external source; of illumination. Pause briefly at phrase boundaries, not after every word.

scenes.title: Step 3 — Stress
scenes.narration: Step three: Stress. Emphasise content words, not every word equally. Notice phenomenon, bioluminescence, organisms, produce light, chemical reactions, and illumination. These carry the main ideas. Keep smaller connecting words lighter.

scenes.title: Step 4 — Connect
scenes.narration: Step four: Connect. The blue highlights show which words should flow together. Link words smoothly within each phrase, with natural pauses where the meaning changes. Avoid robotic word-by-word reading.

scenes.title: Step 5 — Finish
scenes.narration: Step five: Finish. Maintain a steady pace through the final words. Do not rush or trail off. Complete external source of illumination clearly, with controlled pronunciation and a natural ending.

scenes.title: Practice — five difficult scientific sentences
scenes.narration: Now practise these five scientific sentences. Notice challenging vocabulary from bioluminescence, nanotechnology, photosynthesis, neuroplasticity, and thermodynamics. For each sentence, preview, chunk, stress, connect, and finish. Save the reel to practise the method repeatedly.
